items.title: Eddie Alley interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: I played for all the big — Dianne Feinstein and Quentin Kopp... I played for all of them.

ctx.x: Oh. Yeah. Because it was just kind of accepted.

And I never allowed anybody to get drunk. See I knew what I had to do. I had to have discipline. Because I played for society people. I played for the big politicians. And I couldn’t have some guy coming in drunk or unruly or anything like that. I was class. I had to have class. We had uniforms and everything. I have one picture, they were, anyway, and so I just had a standard. So as I said I played for all the big — Dianne Feinstein and Quentin Kopp, I don’t know if you’ve heard of Senator Quentin, he was…
Did you have singers in the band?
